items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia on Nov 15 for answers within 10 days about whether it used shell companies to sell advanced AI chips to China, prioritizing export compliance over Jensen Huang's alleged affair with spy Alice Huang. Megaspeed is suspected of routing chips through Southeast Asia; a Justice Department probe and congressional testimony are underway.
items.title: Bessent Demands Nvidia Compliance Answers Amid China Chip Probe

items.summary: Joshua Wong argues Singapore lacks unsweetened drinks for children and elderly parents. A glass of plain milk has no added sugar, providing about 8g protein and 300mg calcium. With roughly one in 11 adults having diabetes and an ageing population losing muscle and bone, he proposes three steps: the Health Promotion Board adding plain and unsweetened soya milk to its Healthier Dining Programme with a grant; the National Environment Agency making them standard tenancy options like budget meals; and revisiting Nutri-Grade's grading of full-cream milk.
items.title: Forum: Make plain milk an easy, affordable choice at hawker drink stalls

items.summary: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) responds to a letter urging stronger community detection of child abuse, affirming that keeping children safe is shared responsibility. MSF highlights its 2016 Break the Silence campaign, refreshed in August 2025 to reach about 2.4 million people. Its Domestic Violence Trends Report 2026 shows public members accounted for more than 5,100 of 13,475 follow-up reports to NAVH in 2025.
items.title: MSF Responds to Call for Stronger Community Reporting of Child Abuse

items.summary: The Guardian editorial argues that AI alone cannot create a capable civil service, despite calls for reform championed by cabinet secretary Antonia Romeo. While technology may accelerate tasks like identifying at-risk individuals, it cannot deliver homes or substitute adequate resources and trust. The piece highlights declining access to elite posts—56% from privileged families before 1960 versus 45% in 1980-99—and warns of a cultural disconnect that has caused policy blunders.
items.title: Guardian Editorial on Civil Service Reform and AI Limitations

items.summary: The FBI issued a FLASH advisory warning that hackers are weaponizing an open-source, AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks across financial, government, technology, defense, and healthcare sectors since at least August 2026. The tool reduces attack timelines dramatically—some intrusions reach privileged access in under three hours—and enables low-skilled actors to target multiple organizations simultaneously by integrating with external large language models such as Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, and Kimi. As of early November, researchers identified more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles. The advisory highlights campaigns including the October ConnectWise breach attributed to Storm-0940, attacks on South Korean banks exposing roughly 67,000 people's data, a gang that stole about 8.2 million records from over 90 organizations, and Vapor Panda targeting more than 200 organizations across 14 countries.
items.title: FBI Warns ARTEX AI Hacking Tool Is Powering Global Cyberattacks

items.summary: A new IEA Energy Policy Review, published Oct. 5, 2026, finds Spain has strengthened energy security through renewables rising from 35% to 56% of electricity generation between 2015 and 2025 while cutting emissions by about one-fifth. Renewables are lowering wholesale prices and reducing fuel import exposure—without them, gas imports would have been nearly 40%, or USD 26 billion higher in 2024—but fuels still supply almost 70% of total energy consumption. Electrification currently covers just 25% of final energy use versus a 35% target by 2030, with high end-user prices and limited EV adoption slowing progress.
items.title: Spain's Renewable Progress Needs Faster Electrification and Grid Modernization

items.summary: The Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter, that Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive. The report emerged after he discussed with confidants the possibility of returning to lead the company. This development was dated around November 15 and reflects ongoing speculation about leadership at the technology firm.
items.title: Jensen Huang Considering Nvidia CEO Comeback as FT Reports

items.summary: This week's tech roundup covers major leadership, funding, and infrastructure shifts. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO with Colette Kress named interim chief; shares fell nearly 12% in early trading. Anthropic priced its IPO at $70-$78/share (up to $1.4T valuation), below earlier ~$2T hopes. OpenAI closed an $11bn round at a $1.25tn valuation, while Anthropic plans $3.4B on Caterpillar generators for up to 1.7GW of power. Horizon3 hit $100M ARR via its Series E, and AI agents increasingly drive web traffic—Shopify saw orders grow nearly thirteenfold in Q1 2026.
items.title: Weekly Tech Pulse Check: Nvidia Leadership Shake-up and AI Funding Moves

items.summary: COP31 has gained political breathing space after Lula's Brazilian re-election win, Democratic gains in US midterms loosening Trump's grip and possible 2028 White House recovery. Yet threats remain high as projected century heating reaches 2.7°C versus the Paris 1.5°C target. Only UK leader Andy Burnham attended; Guterres warned of make-or-break time. The UN process is vital for a global green transition, though accountability on climate finance and resistance to IPCC undermining are urgent.
items.title: The Guardian editorial on COP31: the green transition must not be derailed

items.summary: Two planes collided Saturday night on a taxiway at Miami International Airport, about an hour after landing: the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a United Parcel Service (UPS) Boeing 767 as they taxied. Two people had minor injuries and received medical treatment. Air traffic controllers reportedly told the UPS crew to yield first; flights were rerouted without disrupting operations, though thousands of delays followed Friday's four-hour FAA ground stop over botched telecom maintenance.
items.title: Planes Collide on Miami Taxiway After Nationwide FAA Ground Stop

items.summary: The What's Next conference, organized by Majority Democrats and funded over two years through a memo circulated by venture capitalist Seth London, gathered center-left Democratic candidates for the 2028 primary. Speakers like Josh Shapiro, Elissa Slotkin and Pete Buttigieg emphasized consensus around cost-cutting bills rather than progressive-versus-moderate divisions. The event drew moderate donors while excluding those pushing leftward moves, elevating supermajority-building candidates over anti-establishment voices. Conflicts centered on leadership—Van Hollen challenged Schumer—and protests disrupted Jeffries by Sunrise Movement organizer Nicole Shea Niebler, age 31, who argued strong progressives were excluded from participation at the scale centrists enjoyed.
items.title: Center-left previews 2028 in Denver

items.summary: Alec Berg, who took over as showrunner of Mike Judge's 'Silicon Valley,' reflects on why the HBO comedy remains uncannily prescient. After spotting a flaw in the pilot—Richard Hendricks buying an unaffordable car—he reshaped it and built the series around mission-driven founders versus exit-obsessed investors. The writers leaned heavily on consultants like Marc Bodnick, Sheryl Sandberg, Jonathan Dotan, and Stanford's Tsachy Weissman to make the show photorealistic, even inventing a compression metric now used by computer scientists. Its 2019 finale, in which founders sabotage an AI too dangerous to release, Berg argues has become harder to imagine today as tech grows darker.
items.title: 'Silicon Valley' Showrunner on How HBO's Comedy Predicted Today's Tech Drama

items.summary: Economist Sanjeev Sanyal warned that Ukraine faces an 'extinction-level drop' in population, with projections suggesting a fall from nearly 50 million in 2000 to just 15.2 million by the end of the century. He noted the country's ageing population means much of this decline may already be difficult to reverse.
items.title: 'Extinction-level drop': Sanjeev Sanyal warns of Ukraine's population collapse

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of defaming India and Prime Minister Narendra Modi at international forums. Advising the opposition leader to stop traveling abroad and instead visit Indian villages if he wished to return to power, Shah warned that following this approach could keep Congress out of government for another 30 years. Speaking in Pune, Maharashtra, he cautioned party workers about Gandhi's current political strategy.
items.title: Amit Shah's Warning to Rahul Gandhi on Foreign Travel and Power

items.summary: ABC NEWS Verify found that Joh Bauch, One Nation's candidate for the outer-Melbourne seat of Sydenham, was one of two administrators of a pro-Pauline Hanson Facebook group called "Make Australia great again with PAULINE HANSON," created July 31, 2026. The other administrator is Down Under News, an account that posted racist material and shared One Nation campaign content. Bauch did not respond to questions; his administrative role was removed after inquiries. A separate Indonesian-based creator, Mmh Shevafeby, also posts in the group. One Nation's spokesperson denied any links to overseas creators ahead of Victoria's November 28 election.
items.title: One Nation denies links to racist Facebook group tied to its Victorian candidate

items.summary: As the Asia-Pacific faces global challenges and economic uncertainty ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, CMG's He Yanke sits down with ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn to discuss regional cooperation. They explore ASEAN's role in the region, open trade, the growing significance of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, and how Free Trade Area 3.0, infrastructure connectivity and the digital economy can drive shared development.
items.title: Exclusive with ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn

items.summary: China's manufacturing sector is undergoing a generational shift as founders hand businesses to the next generation, reshaping both family enterprises and the industry itself. Journalist Bert Hofman, former World Bank country director for China, Mongolia and Korea, joins James Hu, a second-generation factory owner in Shenzhen, to explore how this new generation is transforming their family business and the broader manufacturing landscape behind it.
items.title: Two generations, one Shenzhen business

items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky has urged the United States government and Elon Musk's company to lift speed restrictions on Starshield, a military-grade version of Starlink provided by Washington. He warned that Ukraine cannot intercept Russian jet-powered drones because interceptor connections drop at 161km/h (100mph), leaving it unable to catch faster 'shahed' drones targeting energy infrastructure ahead of winter. Zelensky said the limits have applied only in occupied areas since Monday, adding political weight by implying recognition of those territories as foreign. The dispute has drawn conflicting statements from Musk and President Donald Trump over responsibility. Ukraine also faces a shortage of Patriot interceptors while Russia intensified strikes on its cities. Separately, Estonia announced it would close border crossings with Russia following a suspected GRU-planned arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems.
items.title: Zelensky Urges US and Musk to Lift Starlink Speed Restrictions Ahead of Winter

items.summary: John Allen Rubio was executed Thursday in Huntsville, Texas, for fatally stabbing and beheading his three young children in a 2003 Brownsville apartment. He thanked family before dying via lethal injection of pentobarbital after 21 minutes. His common-law wife Angela Camacho serves life. The killings prompted the site's demolition into a park. Also Thursday, James Pavatt was executed in Oklahoma for killing his girlfriend's estranged husband Rob Andrew; Brenda Andrew fled to Mexico with their two children before arrest. Rubio and Pavatt were the 36th and 37th executions this year, with Florida driving a pace toward surpassing 40.
items.title: Texas Executes Man Who Beheaded Three Children Hours After Oklahoma Execution

items.summary: HMS Vengeance ended a record seven-month (217-day) patrol, surpassing the previous 205-day benchmark set by HMS Vanguard. The submarine carries Britain's Trident missiles and can launch strikes even if land-based systems are destroyed. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting praised the crew as he returned them to Faslane in Scotland. David Cullen of Basic noted patrols exceed the fleet's three-month design, raising concerns about sailor strain and ageing boats amid recruitment difficulties.
items.title: Trident Submarine Concludes Record Seven-Month Deployment

items.summary: In the Women's Super League on Nov 15, London City Lionesses secured a valuable 1-1 draw at Arsenal, keeping them third with 20 points. Goalkeeper Mary Earps made eight saves—her most since 2017—including a dramatic late intervention to deny Frida Maanum and preserve the point after Isobel Goodwin equalised off Alessia Russo's cutback.
items.title: London City Lionesses Hold Arsenal in Third-Place Battle

items.summary: Daniel Stach, one of the Czech Republic's best-known presenters and science journalists, says he will leave his career rather than work under reforms that threaten public broadcasting independence. As hundreds of thousands protest in Prague against right-wing government plans—pushed by populist billionaire Prime Minister Andre Babis—to overhaul media funding, opposition parties liken them to Viktor Orban-era changes in Hungary.
items.title: Czech Presenter Vows to Quit Public TV Over Media Reforms

items.summary: The Port of New Orleans has filed a $1m lawsuit in federal court against the M/V Atlantic Asphalt, its owner Nave Shipping SA and manager Thome Ship Management for colliding with the paddlewheel cruise ship American Heritage on Friday. The crash left 32 people hospitalised but no passengers unaccounted for; about 129 were aboard at the time. Officials called it a 'miracle on the Mississippi.'
items.title: New Orleans port sues tanker owners over cruise ship collision

items.summary: A wildlife rehabilitation centre received a report of venomous vipers sheltering in an underground water meter chamber, but rescuers discovered 19 slow worms instead. The cool, damp concrete structure offered protection from freezing temperatures during winter torpor.
items.title: 19 Slow Worms Mistaken for Vipers Rescued from Water Meter Chamber in Poland

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands gathered in Prague on Sunday afternoon, marking the largest protest yet against Andrej Babiš's three-party government and its plan to replace licence fees with state budget funding for public television and radio. Organised by Million Moments for Democracy under the slogan 'Never again 4:36', the demonstration at Letná drew an estimated 350,000 to 400,000 people who feared loss of editorial independence.
items.title: Prague Rally Opposes Czech Government's Public Media Funding Plan

items.summary: Spain reports nearly 2,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands by boat over a weekend, with more than 13,000 arriving between January and late February. The islands remain one of Europe's main entry points from Africa. Andrew Hilliar of FRANCE 24 provides details and analysis.
items.title: Canary Islands migrant arrivals prompt calls for government action

items.summary: On Thursday, 12 November, dozens of Father Christmas impersonators gathered in south London for a training session organised by the Ministry of Fun to prepare performers for appearances across the UK. Now in its 28th year, Santa School covers sign language greetings, toy trends and sensitive situations such as children wishing for separated parents or sick relatives to recover.
items.title: London's Santa School Trains Father Christmas Performers for 2026 Season

items.summary: At least 20 people were arrested during a "Gen Z regelt" protest march in Berlin on Sunday, November 15, 2026. Riot police clashed with pro-Palestine activists and beat demonstrators inside a subway car amid pyrotechnics; three officers were injured while protesters' injuries went unreported. Slogans targeted Israel and Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Organizers expect around 15,000 in Berlin on November 20 for an Europe-wide youth strike across France, Italy, Spain, Belgium and Great Britain.
items.title: Several Arrested During Gen Z Demonstration in Berlin

items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan congratulated the State of Palestine on its 38th founding anniversary, extending greetings to Palestinians resisting oppression. Türkiye pledges continued defense of the Palestinian cause and advocacy for an independent, sovereign state based on 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as capital. Posted via NSosyal on 15 November 2026.
items.title: Erdogan congratulates Palestine on founding anniversary; reaffirms support for statehood

items.summary: The 20th Francophonie Summit opened Sunday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, gathering leaders from over 80 French-speaking territories. Talks are overshadowed by tensions between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda over their candidates for the new secretary-general, elected Monday for a four-year term. Kinshasa opposes re-electing Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo after eight years and proposed Juliana Lumumba instead; it could withdraw her if Rwanda does likewise.
items.title: Francophonie Summit Opens in Phnom Penh Amid DRC-Rwanda Election Row

items.summary: The World Health Organization warned Friday that respiratory illnesses are surging in Gaza, with more severe cases expected after heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians. Acute respiratory infections rose 33,000 cases above the same period last year, according to WHO representative Dr. Reinhilde Van De Weerdt speaking from Jerusalem. Overcrowding and poor living conditions are driving the increase as Israeli forces advance the Yellow Line under October's ceasefire agreement.
items.title: WHO Warns of Surging Respiratory Illnesses in Gaza Amid Winter Flooding

items.summary: A summit of French-speaking nations opened Sunday in Phnom Penh, with leaders including France's President Emmanuel Macron seeking to avoid a walkout by the group's biggest African member. The Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), resembling the Commonwealth and gathering around 90 states including 53 full members from the Democratic Republic of Congo to Canada, is overshadowed by tensions between Congo President Felix Tshisekedi and Rwanda's Paul Kagame over its new head.
items.title: Francophone Summit Opens in Phnom Penh Amid Congo-Rwanda Clash

items.summary: The Democrats' November 3 midterm victory could enable the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, which would abolish the Electoral College by awarding presidential election outcomes to the national popular vote. The compact requires states totaling 270 electoral votes; so far 222 have joined, and adding Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Nevada—61 combined votes—would activate it.
items.title: How a Democratic Midterm Win Could Trigger National Popular Vote Reform

items.summary: Nvidia, now valued at $3.98 trillion, traces its origins to informal meetings in 1992-1993 between co-founders Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem at a Denny's restaurant in Silicon Valley. The engineers held several-hour-long discussions over coffee—Malachowsky recalled showing up for four hours drinking ten cups—which eventually led staff to move them into a back room also used by San Jose police officers writing reports nearby. Huang had earlier worked as a dishwasher, busboy, and waiter at the chain since age 15. In September 2023, Denny's presented a plaque dedicating the booth to Nvidia; it was briefly removed amid an extramarital scandal but reinstalled within a day.
items.title: The Denny's Where Nvidia Was Conceived and Its Commemorative Plaque

items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia's board to search outside the firm for a new chief executive, citing concerns over internal culture following Jensen Huang's departure. He called for a dramatic shakeup and demanded that Nvidia's board and external legal advisers answer questions about compliance with US export restrictions within 10 days. This follows reports of Huang's relationships and Beijing's denial that Alice Huang was spying.'''
items.title: Bessent Urges Nvidia for External CEO Search Amid Compliance Questions

items.summary: Google plans to disable AI tools by default on school-managed student accounts, beginning in the US before a global rollout. While this restricts general-purpose chatbots, schools are exploring alternatives that teach students about AI and personalize lessons without direct access. Experts like Prof. Karthik Raman of IIT Madras warn that high scores during lessons don't guarantee lasting understanding, recommending tests after gaps or with unfamiliar problems to verify independent learning.
items.title: Google's AI Limits Raise Questions for Schools

items.summary: Darrell Dai, a Nvidia robotics research engineer, announced his resignation via an X post expressing disappointment that engineers were not consulted about leadership changes amid allegations and an ongoing investigation. Praising Jensen Huang's vision for AI and CUDA, Dai said he felt unheard on decisions affecting the company's culture and future. He declined to prejudge the matter, noting some information cannot be shared immediately.
items.title: Nvidia Research Engineer Resigns Over Jensen Huang Departure

items.summary: The Congress party in Jammu and Kashmir demanded a thorough probe into the killing of two special police officers (SPOs), Babi Chand and Rashpal Singh, earlier this week. The party suggested they may have been mistakenly killed by Army personnel during an encounter in Dachhan, Kishtwar district. This remark drew swift condemnation from BJP, which called it provocative. The two SPOs lost their lives while on duty in the region.
items.title: Congress suggests Army ‘friendly fire’ behind deaths of 2 SPOs, BJP calls it 'provocative'

items.summary: For the first time in recent years, Mumbai hosted an online lecture honouring Pakistani Nobel laureate Abdus Salam. The event marked his birth centenary and featured nuclear physicist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy speaking from Islamabad. Organised by the Indian Association of Physics Teachers' Mumbai sub-regional council, it drew physics teachers from Mumbai colleges and TIFR. Hoodbhoy noted Salam's goodwill between India and Pakistan.
items.title: Mumbai Honours Nobel Laureate Abdus Salam on Centenary of His Birth

items.summary: Bitcoin fell toward $62,000 in weekend trading—its weakest level since July—as a gradual decline accelerated into liquidations. Exhaustion is mounting amid the record Binance hack, renewed US political uncertainty after Democratic midterm gains, rising Treasury yields, a stronger dollar, stablecoin outflows of nearly $20 billion over a month, and competition from Anthropic's IPO and AI demand. ETFs saw almost $3 billion in net outflows between Oct. 30 and Nov. 13.
items.title: Crypto's Slow-Motion Selloff Leaves Traders Weary and Hopeless

items.summary: Nine new funds open for subscription in India, eight mutual funds and one SIF by Kotak. Most begin November 16; Bajaj Finserv starts November 20. Minimum applications range from Rs 100 to Rs 50,000 (HDFC Cancer Cure) or Rs 10 lakh (Infinity).
items.title: Nine New Indian Mutual Funds Opening for Subscription (Nov 16–20)

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States raised, for the first time during recent Abu Dhabi peace talks with Russia and Ukrainian representatives, whether Ukraine would withdraw from its eastern Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership. Zelenskyy described this as an extremely difficult issue, noting that Moscow has repeatedly treated NATO's eastward expansion as a security threat—citing it among Putin's justifications for the February 2022 invasion—and has made Ukrainian withdrawal from Donbas a condition for peace. Kyiv insists any territorial compromise requires comprehensive security guarantees modeled on Article 5 of the NATO treaty, military support and financial assistance, plus approval in a national referendum; Zelenskyy reaffirmed that Ukraine will not voluntarily surrender its territory.
items.title: US Raises Unprecedented Donbas Proposal Linking Ukraine's NATO Membership to Territorial Concessions

items.summary: Jammu Police have foiled an alleged cheating racket during the Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board (JKSSB) Finance Assistant Examination held on November 15. Acting on intelligence inputs, police deployed multiple teams around examination centres and apprehended as many as 14 suspected facilitators from peripheral locations before the exam began. Several electronic devices, including wireless radio sets allegedly used to transmit answers, were seized. Three FIRs have been registered at Domana Police Station, and a Special Investigation Team has been constituted to probe the entire network.
items.title: Jammu Police Foil JKSSB Exam Cheating Racket; 14 Apprehended with Electronic Devices

items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate seized 355 plots at the Vitthal Greens real estate project linked to Chaitanya Baghel, son of former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel. The action relates to an alleged Rs 2,883-crore liquor scam (2019-2023). Of the project's 385 total plots, 30 were already sold and excluded; seized properties are valued at around Rs 61 crore. Bhupesh Baghel questioned the timing as tribunal proceedings continue.
items.title: Enforcement Directorate Seizes Vitthal Greens Plots in Chaitanya Baghel Liquor Scam Case

items.summary: On the first day of nominations for gram panchayat polls across 23 urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh, more than 10,500 applications were filed. The state election commission recorded 9,036 total nominations: 3,282 for sarpanch posts and 5,754 for ward members. Ananthapur district led with 309 sarpanch nominations, while Palnadu topped the ward category with 696.
items.title: Nomination surge and TD's ULB candidate list in Andhra Pradesh elections

items.summary: "Immune boosting" has become an online trend, promoted through recipes, nutrition books and naturopathic clinics. Researchers Alessandro Marcon of the University of Alberta's Health Law Institute and Jia Hu of the University of British Columbia studied this discourse during COVID-19. They found it problematic: content often contains scientific inaccuracies about immunity while promoting ineffective products or services. Their Instagram research showed more than 96% of reviewed immune-boosting content came from creators selling products, with companies tagged in a sample of posts. The authors argue the immune system needs balance and maintenance rather than enhancement, warning that commercialization can erode trust in evidence-based interventions like vaccines.
items.title: Popular 'immune-boosting' ideas may be more hindrance than help

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned that a depression over the west-central Bay of Bengal would strengthen into a cyclonic storm by evening November 16 and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, before moving toward the Andhra Pradesh coast within two days. As of late on November 15, the system was centered near latitude 10.2°N and longitude 86.8°E, about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka) and roughly 920-1,030 km from Chennai, Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu sought urgent central financial assistance after Cyclone Murasu caused an estimated ₹2,484.43 crore in damage across Bapatla, Palnadu, Eluru and East Godavari districts. A seven-member Central team led by Joint Secretary Chittaranjan Das inspected nearly 60 locations of damaged fields, roads and houses. Naidu attributed the widespread destruction to El Niño conditions combined with two cyclones striking in quick succession.
items.title: Depression over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into severe cyclonic storm by Nov 17, move towards Andhra Pradesh coast: IMD

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is traveling to Manila on November 16, 2025, for a three-day trip spanning November 15-17 to attend the annual India-ASEAN Summit and East Asia Summit. US President Donald Trump, Brazil's Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Canada's Mark Carney, and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov are also expected to participate. The summit emphasizes strengthening maritime security ties, expanding economic partnerships, addressing conflicts including Myanmar, and reviewing trade agreements amid India-ASEAN annual trade of about $122 billion.
items.title: Modi and Trump Set for ASEAN Summit in Manila Amid Maritime and Economic Focus

items.summary: In Fazilka, Punjab, five people including three minors were killed and 11 others injured when a car carrying all 16 occupants from a wedding collided with a pickup near village Theh Kalandar on Sunday evening. Two victims remained critical and were referred to other hospitals while the rest received treatment at the Government Hospital in Fazilka. Local residents helped rescue trapped passengers before ambulances arrived.
items.title: Wedding Party Car Crash in Fazilka Kills Five

items.summary: Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh performed a live concert in Indore on Sunday despite attempts to prevent his visit. The 42-year-old recited couplets from late Urdu poet Rahat Indori, including “kisi ke baap ka Hindostan thodi hai,” and urged the audience to chant ‘Jai Shri Mahakal.’ Earlier, emails threatening bomb blasts had been sent to the mayor’s office, three banks and three private schools. Police later described these messages as prima facie fake after investigation.
items.title: Diljit Dosanjh Defies Opposition in Indore Concert

items.summary: Police arrested two suspects, Mahakdeep Kaur and Devendra Singh from Gurdaspur, Punjab on November 14 for the November 3 Ramsinghpur railway blast. Preliminary probes allege they were directed by Pakistani handlers linked to ISI, who supplied timer bombs; one failed attempt occurred October 12-13 before the successful attack at around 9:45 pm.
items.title: Rajasthan Rail Blast Suspects Arrested in Punjab with Alleged Pakistan Links

items.summary: The All India Trinamool Congress (TMC), led by Mamata Banerjee, submitted affidavits to the Election Commission on Sunday in a dispute over party control triggered by Ritabrata Banerjee's rival faction. TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee accused rivals of forging signatures through police intimidation across West Bengal and threatened prosecution. His side cited support from 17 MPs, 32 MLAs in West Bengal, five MLAs in Meghalaya, one MLA in Assam, plus over two lakh grassroots affidavits—challenging Ritabrata's claim of 65 MLAs.
items.title: Battle for TMC Control: Mamata Camp Submits Affidavits Amid Allegations of Forged Support

items.summary: Former AAP Rajya Sabha leader Raghav Chadha has been appointed to the Punjab BJP's manifesto committee ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. Former president Avinash Rai Khanna heads the 13-member panel, joined by defectors Manpreet Singh Badal and Ashwani Sharma among others. Sunil Jakhar leads a separate chargesheet committee targeting the AAP government. The appointments come as BJP explores reviving its alliance with SAD for early-2027 polls across all 117 seats.
items.title: Raghav Chadha gets key role in Punjab BJP's manifesto panel ahead of 2027 assembly polls

items.summary: On Sunday, two men suspected of cattle smuggling were killed during an alleged gunfight with police in Nuh district, Haryana. A third suspect and a police officer were injured; the survivor was hospitalized. The Crime Investigation Agency team at Firozpur Jhirka received information about the smuggling on Sunday morning and set up a barricade to intercept the vehicle. Police allege that the suspects opened fire first, prompting an exchange of shots.
items.title: Two Suspected Cattle Smugglers Killed in Gunfight with Police in Haryana's Nuh District

items.summary: Police are investigating cab driver S Indushekar's alleged killing of seven members of his wife's family over roughly 15 days in October, examining whether a property dispute worth an estimated Rs 3 crore was a motive. Investigators look into allegations that he tried to control family documents and sold or pledged gold jewellery taken from victims, possibly using proceeds for body disposal costs. A promise allegedly made to his 17-year-old daughter about her mother's share may have influenced her role in disposing of bodies. The couple had been married nearly 20 years amid reported friction over the wife's ties to her family. Indushekar, 52, is accused of using a grinding stone and transporting victims across Karnataka and Tamil Nadu before their recovery.
items.title: Bengaluru Family Killings Probe Explores Property Dispute and Gold Sales as Motives

items.summary: A video circulating on social media claims that Khalistani supporters caused a disturbance during Diwali in Canada. The claim is described as recent, but the video itself has been identified as three years old.
items.title: Canada Diwali Riots Video Is Three Years Old
